title: Using Evidence, Improving Quality, Reporting Errors

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already follow protocols, and your PCRs may already be reviewed. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Find, appraise and apply evidence in five steps
  2. Tell research from quality management; use PDSA, metrics and indicators
  3. Recognize and report adverse events and near misses

Textbook: Chapter 11, PDF pages 836–867
slides.say: Welcome back. Last class we learned how studies are built. Today we use them, and then look at how your service checks its own care. As an EMR you already follow protocols, and your reports may already be reviewed. As a PCP you carry more drugs and make more decisions, so quality and safety matter even more. We'll cover three things: the five steps of evidence-based practice; the difference between research and quality management, with tools like the PDSA cycle, metrics and indicators; and patient safety, meaning adverse events, near misses, and why you report both.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课学了研究是怎么做出来的；今天我们来用研究，再看你的服务怎样检查自己的照护。当 EMR 时你已经按流程做事，你的报告可能也被审核过。作为 PCP，你带的药更多、要做的决定更多，所以质量和安全更加重要。今天讲三件事：循证实践的五个步骤；研究和质量管理的区别，以及 PDSA 循环、metric 和 indicator 这些工具；还有患者安全，也就是不良事件、险兆，以及为什么两者都要上报。

slides.title: Evidence-based practice: five steps
slides.body:
1. Ask: an answerable question (PICO)
  2. Search: the best evidence, efficiently
  3. Appraise: valid? useful in my setting?
  4. Apply: put it into practice
  5. Evaluate: did the change work?

EBP = using research, not doing it. ILCOR now reviews resuscitation evidence continuously, not every 5 years.
slides.say: Evidence-based practice, or EBP, means carefully using the current best evidence when you make decisions for individual patients. It's about using research, not running studies. There are five steps. Ask: turn a vague idea into an answerable question with PICO. Search: find the best evidence efficiently. Appraise: is it valid, and useful in my setting? Apply it to practice. Then evaluate: did the change work? Medicine moves fast. ILCOR, the International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation, used to release guidelines every five years; now it reviews evidence continuously. So EBP is lifelong, and one paramedic can still push a whole system to change.
slides.sayZh: 循证实践，也就是 EBP，指在为个体病人做决定时，审慎地运用当前最佳证据。它讲的是用研究，不是自己做研究。一共五步。提问：用 PICO 把模糊的想法变成能回答的问题。检索：高效地找到最佳证据。评价：它可信吗？在我的场景里有用吗？应用到实践中。然后评估：这个改变有效吗？医学变得很快。国际复苏联络委员会 ILCOR 以前每五年发布一次指南，现在持续评审证据。所以循证实践是终身的，一个救护员也可以推动整个系统改变。

slides.title: Searching smart
slides.body:
WhereWhat you get
Cochrane, PEP, BestBETsalready appraised; may be out of date
PubMed (Medline), EMBASE, CINAHLoriginal, mostly peer-reviewed studies
Googlegrey literature: not peer-reviewed
  • OR joins synonyms (wider); AND joins PICO parts (narrower)
  • Wildcard: paramed* finds paramedic, paramedics, paramedicine
slides.say: Where do you look? When time is short, start where someone has already appraised the evidence: the Cochrane library of systematic reviews, Canada's prehospital evidence project, called PEP, and BestBETs. The catch: on a hot topic they may be out of date. For original studies, search databases like PubMed, EMBASE or CINAHL. Plain Google finds grey literature, which isn't peer-reviewed but gives an overview. Use Boolean operators. Join synonyms with OR to widen the search, like paramedic OR ambulance OR EMS. Join the PICO parts with AND to narrow it. A wildcard, like paramed with a star, catches every ending.
slides.sayZh: 去哪里找？时间紧时，先从别人已经评价过证据的地方开始：Cochrane 系统综述库、加拿大院前循证项目 PEP，以及 BestBETs。缺点是热门话题可能过时。要找原始研究，就检索 PubMed、EMBASE 或 CINAHL 这类数据库。直接用 Google 搜到的是灰色文献，没有经过同行评审，但能帮你了解概况。要用布尔运算符：同义词之间用 OR 连接来扩大范围，比如 paramedic OR ambulance OR EMS；PICO 各部分之间用 AND 连接来缩小范围。像 paramed 加星号这样的通配符，能抓到所有词尾。

slides.title: Appraising a study
slides.body:
1. What was the question (PICO)? Close to mine?
  2. What design? Look in the methods
  3. Was it the right design for the question?
  • Check Table 1: were the groups alike at the start?
  • External validity is your call: are they like your patients?
  • Published ≠ good: publication bias hides dull or negative results
slides.say: Found a study? Start with three questions. What was its research question, and is it close to yours? What design did it use? Look in the methods section. And was that the right design for the question? Then check internal validity. Most papers have a table of baseline characteristics, often Table 1. Were the groups similar in age, sex and medical history? If not, did the authors adjust for it, or discuss it as a limitation? External validity is your call: are these patients like yours? Finally, published doesn't mean good. Dull or negative results are less often submitted or printed. That's publication bias.
slides.sayZh: 找到一篇研究？先问三个问题：它的研究问题是什么，和你的问题接近吗？用了什么设计？看方法部分。这个设计适合这个问题吗？然后查内部效度。多数论文都有一张基线特征表，常常是表 1：两组在年龄、性别、病史上相似吗？如果不相似，作者有没有做统计校正，或在局限性里讨论？外部效度要你自己判断：这些病人像你的病人吗？最后，发表了不代表好。结果平淡或阴性的研究更少被投稿或刊登，这叫发表偏倚。

slides.title: Levels and direction of evidence
slides.body:
Level Iat least one proper RCT, or a review of RCTsstrongest
Level IIcomparison group, not randomized (incl. registries)middle
Level IIIno comparison group, simulation, or animal studyweakest

Add a direction: supportive, opposing, or neutral. Sum it up in a CAT with a clinical bottom line.
slides.say: With several studies, how do you weigh them? Canada's PEP project grades evidence in three levels. Level one: at least one properly randomized controlled trial, or a systematic review that includes them. Level two: a comparison group but no randomization, including registry studies that compare groups. Level three: no comparison group, or a simulation or animal study. Then add a direction: supportive, opposing, or neutral when there was no significant difference. The ladder isn't perfect: a well-run observational study can beat a poor RCT, and satisfaction questions suit qualitative research better. Sum it all up in a critically appraised topic, or CAT, ending with a clinical bottom line.
slides.sayZh: 手上有好几篇研究，怎么权衡？加拿大 PEP 项目把证据分三级。一级：至少一项规范的随机对照试验，或包含它们的系统综述。二级：有对照组但没有随机分组，包括有比较的登记研究。三级：没有对照组，或是模拟、动物研究。然后标上方向：支持、反对，或没有显著差异时标为中性。这个阶梯并不完美：做得好的观察研究可能胜过做得差的 RCT，满意度类问题更适合定性研究。最后把一切汇总成批判性评价主题，也就是 CAT，以临床结论收尾。

slides.q: You find a study comparing patients treated by crews who carried a new device with patients treated by crews who didn't. Patients were not randomized. On the Canadian PEP scale, what level of evidence is this?
options: It can't be graded, because it isn't an RCT
slides.say: Let's check. You find a study comparing patients treated by crews who carried a new device with patients treated by crews who didn't. The patients were not randomized. On the Canadian PEP scale, what level of evidence is this? A, level one. B, level two. C, level three. D, it can't be graded, because it isn't an RCT. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检查一下。你找到一项研究，比较配了新设备的救护组接诊的病人和没配的救护组接诊的病人，病人没有随机分组。按加拿大 PEP 量表，这是几级证据？A 一级；B 二级；C 三级；D 无法分级，因为它不是 RCT。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, level two. There's a comparison group but no randomization, which is exactly PEP level two. Level one needs at least one properly randomized trial, or a systematic review of them. Level three is for studies with no comparison group, simulations, or animal research. D is wrong because the scale is designed to grade non-randomized studies too.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，二级。有对照组，但没有随机分组，正是 PEP 二级。一级需要至少一项规范的随机试验，或它们的系统综述；三级是没有对照组的研究、模拟或动物研究。D 错，因为这个量表本来就设计成也给非随机研究分级。

slides.title: Research or quality management?
slides.body:
ResearchQuality management
Goalnew knowledge for all patientsbetter care here
REB approvalrequirednot required
Timeoften longimmediate, repeated
  • Quality management = QA + QI + programme evaluation
  • Unsure? Ask your local REB chair
slides.say: Research and quality management can use the same data and methods, so how do you tell them apart? Look at how the results will be used. Research aims for new knowledge for all patients, everywhere, and needs research ethics board approval. Quality management aims to improve care in your own service. It doesn't need REB review, though it must still be ethical. It has three parts. Quality assurance, or QA, regularly checks care against the standard. When QA finds a gap, quality improvement, or QI, tries to fix it. Programme evaluation asks whether a specific programme works. Unsure which one a project is? Ask your local REB chair.
slides.sayZh: 研究和质量管理可以用同样的数据和方法，那怎么区分？看结果拿来做什么。研究追求适用于所有地方、所有病人的新知识，需要研究伦理委员会批准。质量管理是为了改进你自己服务里的照护，不需要 REB 审查，但仍然必须合乎伦理。它包括三部分：质量保证 QA，定期对照标准检查照护；QA 发现差距时，质量改进 QI 设法弥补；项目评估看某个具体项目有没有效。拿不准一个项目属于哪一类？问本地 REB 的主席。

slides.title: Structure, process, outcome
slides.body:
Structurevehicles, equipment, staffing, trainingwhat you work with
Processprotocols followed, assessment, treatmentwhat you do
Outcomethe patient's resulting conditionwhat happens to the patient

A glucometer that keeps failing is a structure problem; retraining crews won't fix it.
slides.say: To judge quality, services look at three linked parts. Structure is what you work with: vehicles, equipment, staffing, and clinicians' training and qualifications. Process is what's actually done: following protocols, assessing, treating. Outcome is what happens to the patient as a result. Improve structure and process, and outcomes should follow. This framework points to the real cause of a problem. If a glucometer keeps giving errors, that's a structure problem. Retraining crews won't fix it, but repairing or replacing the device will. If crews skip a reassessment, that's a process problem.
slides.sayZh: 评价质量时，服务会看三个相互关联的部分。结构是你用来工作的东西：车辆、设备、人员配置，以及医护人员的培训和资质。过程是实际做了什么：执行流程、评估、治疗。结局是病人因此出现的结果。改善结构和过程，结局就应随之改善。这个框架能指向问题的真正原因。如果血糖仪老是报错，那是结构问题；再培训救护组没用，修或换设备才行。如果救护组漏掉复评，那才是过程问题。

slides.title: The PDSA cycle
slides.body:
Plan→Do→Study→Act
  • Plan: e.g. > 90% of fluid boluses reassessed every 500 mL
  • Do: audit PCRs, find causes, give feedback
  • Study: did we reach the goal?
  • Act: met → new target; missed → change the plan

Care didn't follow protocol? Education first, then look for system barriers.
slides.say: Many services run quality improvement with the PDSA cycle: plan, do, study, act. Here's a PCP example. The BC hypovolemia protocol says to reassess after every five hundred millilitres of fluid. Plan: set a goal, say more than ninety percent of fluid boluses with a documented reassessment. Do: audit patient care reports, find out why the step was missed, and give crews feedback, or even change the protocol. Study: was the goal reached? Act: if yes, set a new target; if not, change the plan and go around again. When an audit finds care that didn't follow protocol, the first step is usually education, plus a look for system barriers.
slides.sayZh: 很多服务用 PDSA 循环做质量改进：计划、执行、研究、行动。举个 PCP 的例子。BC 低血容量流程要求每输五百毫升液体就复评一次。计划：定一个目标，比如超过百分之九十的补液都有复评记录。执行：审核病人照护报告，找出漏做的原因，给救护组反馈，甚至修改流程。研究：目标达到了吗？行动：达到了就定新目标；没达到就改方案，再转一圈。审核发现照护没按流程做时，第一步通常是教育，同时查一查有没有系统障碍。

slides.title: Metrics, indicators, scorecards
slides.body:
• Metric: a simple number, e.g. boluses with a reassessment
  • Indicator: a metric tied to a target, e.g. > 90%
  • Response time: 9-1-1 call at dispatch → first unit on scene
  • Common indicator: > 90% of responses in ≤ 8.5 minutes
  • Balanced scorecard: service, operations, finance, learning
slides.say: Quality management runs on numbers. A metric is a simple statistic that stands for something important, like the number of boluses with a documented reassessment. An indicator is a metric tied to a target, like more than ninety percent. The classic example is response time, measured from when the nine-one-one call reaches dispatch to when the first paramedic unit arrives. A common indicator: more than ninety percent of responses in eight and a half minutes or less. Big swings from the target get investigated. Some services use a balanced scorecard, with targets in four equal areas: customer service, operations, finance, and innovation and learning.
slides.sayZh: 质量管理靠数字运转。metric 是代表某件重要事情的简单统计，比如有复评记录的补液次数。indicator 是绑定了目标的 metric，比如超过百分之九十。经典例子是反应时间：从 911 电话到达调度中心，到第一辆救护单位到场。常见的 indicator 是：超过百分之九十的反应在八点五分钟以内。明显偏离目标的波动要调查。有的服务用平衡计分卡，在四个同等重要的领域设目标：客户服务、运营、财务、创新与学习。

slides.title: Patient safety: adverse event or near miss?
slides.body:
Adverse eventNear miss
care caused harm, not the illnesscould have caused harm, caught in time
report to patient, receiving staff, your servicereport it too
  • Types: system, no-fault, cognitive errors (may overlap)
  • Canada, 2004: 7.5% of hospital patients had an adverse event
slides.say: Patient safety is the close cousin of quality management. Its goal is to reduce harm caused by our own care. A Canadian study published in two thousand four estimated that seven point five percent of hospital patients had an adverse event, and about seventy thousand a year suffered preventable harm. There's no reason to think prehospital care is safer. An adverse event is harm caused by care, not by the patient's condition. It may be a system error, where the setup allowed it; a no-fault error, which couldn't be predicted or prevented; or a cognitive error, from a clinician's decision. A near miss could have caused harm, but was caught in time.
slides.sayZh: 患者安全是质量管理的近亲，目标是减少我们自己的照护造成的伤害。二〇〇四年发表的一项加拿大研究估计，百分之七点五的住院病人发生过不良事件，每年约七万人受到本可预防的伤害。没有理由认为院前更安全。不良事件是照护造成的伤害，而不是病人本身病情造成的。它可能是系统错误，也就是系统让它有机会发生；可能是无过错错误，无法预测、无法预防；也可能是认知错误，出自医护人员的决定。险兆是本可能造成伤害、但及时被发现的错误。

slides.q: While you manage a patient's airway, his IV fluid runs in much faster than you planned. He now has new crackles and is more short of breath. After treating him, what should you do?
options: Nothing more: he's improving, so no report is needed
Tell the patient and receiving staff, and report it to your service
Report it only if the hospital complains
Record it as a near miss, since he's fine now
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. While you manage a patient's airway, his IV fluid runs in much faster than you planned. He now has new crackles and is more short of breath. After treating him, what should you do? A, nothing more; he's improving, so no report is needed. B, tell the patient and the receiving staff, and report it to your service. C, report it only if the hospital complains. D, record it as a near miss, since he's fine now. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一道 PCP 决策题。你正在处理病人的气道，他的静脉输液比计划快得多地输了进去。现在他出现新的湿啰音，气更急了。处理好他之后，你应该怎么做？A 不用再做什么，他在好转，不需要上报；B 告诉病人和接收的医护人员，并向你的服务上报；C 只有医院投诉时才上报；D 记为险兆，因为他现在没事。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Fluid overload from the IV is harm caused by care, not by his illness, so it's an adverse event. You're responsible for telling the patient, the receiving health care providers, and your organization. A and C hide an error the system needs to learn from. D is wrong because a near miss is caught before it reaches the patient; this one reached him and caused harm. Reporting also lets the service look for a system fix.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。输液造成的液体过负荷是照护带来的伤害，不是他的病造成的，所以是不良事件。你有责任告诉病人、接收的医护人员和你的机构。A 和 C 隐瞒了系统需要从中学习的错误。D 错，因为险兆是在到达病人之前就被发现；这次已经到达病人并造成了伤害。上报也让服务有机会找到系统层面的改进办法。

slides.title: Report, learn, fix the system
slides.body:
• Report every adverse event and near miss
  • Anonymous reporting: disclose without fear of discipline
  • Reports drive fixes: reorganized drug kits, colour labels
  • Field risks: poor light, too many or too few people, little backup
  • Safety huddles, M&M rounds: learn together, keep it confidential
slides.say: Why report errors, even harmless ones? Because patient safety focuses on the system, not on blaming a person. Paramedics are generally doing their best, but we work in poor light, with crowds or too few hands, and little backup, and those conditions breed errors. To encourage honesty, more services offer anonymous reporting, so you can disclose without fear of discipline. Reports lead to fixes. If two vials look alike and sit side by side, the service can reorganize the drug kit and add colour-coded labels. Patient safety huddles and morbidity and mortality rounds let crews learn together, with patient details kept confidential.
slides.sayZh: 为什么连没造成伤害的错误也要报？因为患者安全关注的是系统，而不是责怪个人。救护员通常已经尽力，但我们常在光线差、人太多或人手太少、支援也少的环境里工作，这些条件最容易出错。为了鼓励诚实，越来越多的服务提供匿名上报，你可以说出错误而不用担心处分。上报会带来改进：两种药瓶长得像又放在一起，服务就可以重新整理药包，贴上颜色标签。患者安全碰头会和发病率与死亡率讨论会，让大家一起学习，并对病人信息保密。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• Checks name, dose, concentration, route before every drug
  • Asks the partner to double-check, especially new PCP drugs
  • Writes PCRs that an audit can actually use
  • Takes audit feedback as a lesson; flags system barriers
  • Reports and discloses errors; joins safety huddles

BC PCP-only exam drugs: D10W, dexamethasone, dimenhydrinate, diphenhydramine, ipratropium, ondansetron, TXA
slides.say: So what changes for you as a PCP? Your drug list grows. In BC, seven exam drugs are PCP-only: D10W, dexamethasone, dimenhydrinate, diphenhydramine, ipratropium, ondansetron and TXA. Add IV fluids, and there are many more chances for a mix-up. So before every drug, check the name, dose, concentration and route, and have your partner double-check when you can. Your patient care reports are the raw material of every audit, so write them clearly and completely. Treat audit feedback as a lesson, and speak up about system barriers. And when something goes wrong, report it and disclose it honestly.
slides.sayZh: 那么作为 PCP，你有什么变化？你的药物清单变长了。在 BC，有七种考纲药物只有 PCP 能用：D10W、地塞米松、茶苯海明、苯海拉明、异丙托溴铵、昂丹司琼和 TXA。再加上静脉输液，出错的机会多了很多。所以每次给药前，核对药名、剂量、浓度和途径，能让搭档复核就让搭档复核。你的病人照护报告是每次审核的原材料，要写得清楚完整。把审核反馈当作学习，并说出系统里的障碍。出了差错，要上报，并诚实告知。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Look-alike vials stored side by side
  • Dark, crowded, rushed scenes: slow down for the drug check
  • “No harm done” still means report it (near miss)
  • QI aiming at knowledge for others? That's research → REB
  • Evidence summaries: check the date and the source
slides.say: A few new hazards to watch. First, look-alike vials. If two drugs look the same and sit close together, report it before it hurts someone. Second, the scene itself. Poor light, crowds and time pressure are exactly when drug checks get skipped, so slow down for that one step. Third, no harm done doesn't mean nothing to report: a near miss is still a report. Fourth, if your team's improvement project starts aiming at new knowledge for other services, it's becoming research and needs ethics board approval. Fifth, when you look up evidence, check the date and the source.
slides.sayZh: 有几个新的风险要注意。第一，外观相似的药瓶。两种药长得像又放得近，在它伤到人之前就上报。第二，现场本身。光线差、人多、时间紧，正是最容易跳过药物核对的时候，所以这一步一定要慢下来。第三，没造成伤害不等于没东西可报：险兆照样要报。第四，如果你们团队的改进项目开始追求给其他服务用的新知识，就变成了研究，需要伦理委员会批准。第五，查证据时看清日期和来源。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. EBP: ask (PICO), search, appraise, apply, evaluate
  2. Quality management improves care here (no REB); research is for everyone (REB)
  3. Report every adverse event and near miss; fix systems, not blame

Next: Chapter 12, expanded EMS systems and community paramedicine
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: evidence-based practice has five steps: ask with PICO, search, appraise, apply, and evaluate. Use pre-appraised sources when time is short, and grade studies by level and direction. Two: quality management improves care in your own service and doesn't need ethics board approval; research builds knowledge for everyone and does. Three: report every adverse event and every near miss, and disclose adverse events to the patient, the receiving staff and your service. Next class, Chapter twelve: community paramedicine and the expanding roles of paramedics across Canada. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，循证实践五步：用 PICO 提问、检索、评价、应用、评估；时间紧时用预先评价过的资源，并按等级和方向给研究定级。二，质量管理改进的是你自己服务里的照护，不需要伦理委员会批准；研究是为所有人建立知识，需要批准。三，每一个不良事件和每一个险兆都要上报，不良事件要告知病人、接收的医护人员和你的服务。下节课进入第十二章：社区院前医学，以及救护员在全加拿大不断扩展的角色。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
